title: A Comprehensive Tutorial and Survey of Business-Outcome-Driven Private 5G/6G Networks: Exploring Enterprise Intent, Economic-Aware Control, Deployment Options, Use Cases, and Challenges
affiliations: , Celona Inc., Chongqing University and NIT, Warangal

detail.title: A Comprehensive Tutorial and Survey of Business-Outcome-Driven Private 5G/6G Networks: Exploring Enterprise Intent, Economic-Aware Control, Deployment Options, Use Cases, and Challenges
detail.abstract: Private fifth-generation (5G) and future sixthgeneration (6G) networks are moving from experimental connectivity platforms into operational infrastructure for factories, ports, warehouses, hospitals, mines, campuses, utilities, airports, and other enterprise environments. However, most network intelligence still optimizes technical key performance indicators (KPIs), such as latency, throughput, reliability, availability, coverage, jitter, energy efficiency, spectrum utilization, and slicelevel service level objectives. These quantities are necessary, but they are not the final objective of enterprise deployment. Enterprise decision makers care about production output, downtime avoidance, worker safety, energy cost, logistics flow, asset utilization, regulatory compliance, risk exposure, and return on investment (ROI). This mismatch creates a semantic, economic, causal, and governance gap between business objectives and network-control actions. This article provides a comprehensive tutorial and survey of business-outcome-driven private 5G/6G networks. We synthesize private-network architectures, nonpublic network (NPN) management, intent-based networking, autonomous-network standards, Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) service management and orchestration (SMO), RAN intelligent controllers (RICs), network slicing, edge computing, digital twins, knowledge graphs, large language models (LLMs), agentic artificial intelligence (AI), and economic-aware optimization. We introduce a layered abstraction in which business intent is transformed into operational intent, service intent, network intent, resource-control action, and measurable business outcome feedback. We further develop a reference architecture for Enterprise Network Intelligence, identify the role of Business Intent Languages (BILs), define the KPI-to-outcome translation problem, present economic objective formulations, analyze deployment models and use cases, survey datasets and testbeds, and derive research challenges. The central thesis is that future private networks should not merely automate network operations; they should become governed enterprise decision systems that optimize communication, computing, sensing, and operational resources according to business value.

title: When Is Data Annotation Participatory? A Comparative Study of Authority in AI Data Work
affiliations: and Pennsylvania State University

detail.title: When Is Data Annotation Participatory? A Comparative Study of Authority in AI Data Work
detail.abstract: Despite growing calls for "participatory AI" in response to concerns about bias, labor exploitation, and accountability, participation is often invoked without specifying whether it meaningfully redistributes power. In data annotation, participatory language frequently functions as legitimizing rhetoric, even as authority over problem framing, workflows, and downstream use remains centralized. This paper examines when, and under what conditions, data annotation can be considered genuinely participatory. We present a comparative analysis of six data annotation initiatives across commercial, academic, and community-driven contexts using an integrative framework that distinguishes between epistemic, procedural, and governance authority in data annotation. Drawing on deductive coding of organizational documents, we analyze how participatory claims are operationalized in practice. Across cases, we identify three recurring participation configurations: commercial crowdwork, institutional volunteerism, and community collaboration, that differ systematically in how authority is distributed. We find that genuine participation does not arise from human involvement, ethical labor conditions, domain expertise, or transparency alone, but from structural conditions that redistribute authority over problem framing, annotation practices, and control beyond the point of data production. We reframe participation as a question of authority distribution rather than labor inclusion, with implications for democratic accountability in AI governance.

title: The Epistemology of Unaffiliated Research: A Theoretical Framework for Measuring, Validating, and Preserving Independent Knowledge Creation

detail.title: The Epistemology of Unaffiliated Research: A Theoretical Framework for Measuring, Validating, and Preserving Independent Knowledge Creation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: For refinement purposes, free resources have been used. The author declares no competing interests. The paper is based on the author's own experience and thoughts.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical/conceptual paper and did not involve human participants, animal subjects, or identifiable personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework for recognizing, measuring, and preserving research output generated entirely outside institutional structures. Drawing from the documented case of an independent researcher who produced a substantial body of publicly documented research without institutional funding, research staff, or proprietary infrastructure, we propose a new paradigm for validating unaffiliated knowledge creation. We introduce the concept of "Unaffiliated Researcher Temples"-decentralized physical and digital repositories designed to preserve grassroots innovations and establish intellectual sovereignty for independent creators. We examine transformative policy innovations by leaders who emerged from non-elite institutional backgrounds as compelling evidence that profound intellectual contributions do not require prestigious academic credentials. The framework challenges traditional hierarchies of knowledge production by establishing an epistemology of lived experience, demonstrating that profound intellectual contributions emerge not only from institutional abundance but also from individual necessity, self-reliance, and practical intelligence. We argue that independent research activity can be documented, examined, and evaluated through transparent public records, meeting the criteria for formal recognition within global achievement frameworks. This paper contributes to decolonizing knowledge systems by validating street-level epistemology and proposing sustainable governance models through Decentralized Science (DeSci) principles and community-based stewardship.

title: The Inference-Compute Frontier and a Latency-Efficient Architecture for Limit Order Book Prediction
affiliations: Independent Researcher, USA.

detail.title: The Inference-Compute Frontier and a Latency-Efficient Architecture for Limit Order Book Prediction
detail.abstract: We study whether a scaling-law-style inference-compute frontier appears in limit order book prediction. Using FI-2010 and a suite of models ranging from small decision trees to neural LOB architectures, we find that the realized empirical frontier of predictive loss versus structural forward work is well summarized by a power law. In particular, with MLPLOB held out as an architecture family, a power-law fit to the low- and mid-compute non-MLPLOB frontier extrapolates across multiple orders of magnitude and attains 𝑅 2 = 0.941 on the excluded high-compute MLPLOB target frontier. A similar exercise in latency space gives substantially weaker results, showing that latency is not merely noisy compute. We use this gap to motivate FastBiNLOB, a dense axis-separable LOB mixer built from hardware-friendly temporal and feature mixing operations. In a five-seed experiment, FastBiNLOB exceeds the published 𝑦10 and 𝑦100 macro-F1 targets at notably lower latency than existing published SOTA architectures.

title: Beyond Bretton Woods: Dollar Hegemony, Institutional Fracture, and the Architecture of a Multipolar Global Financial Order
affiliations: University of Benin

detail.title: Beyond Bretton Woods: Dollar Hegemony, Institutional Fracture, and the Architecture of a Multipolar Global Financial Order
detail.abstract:
The post-war Bretton Woods architecture, constructed in the shadow of catastrophic geopolitical failure and designed for an economy in which the United States accounted for nearly half of global industrial output, has proven resistant to reform even as the structural conditions that justified its design have dissolved. Eighty years after the Bretton Woods conference, the International Monetary Fund retains a voting structure in which the United States alone commands a de facto blocking minority; the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) remains simultaneously a technical chokepoint, a geopolitical instrument, and a barrier to financial inclusion for the developing world; and the dollar continues to constitute 57.4 per cent of global foreign exchange reserves despite the United States accounting for approximately 25 per cent of global GDP. This paper interrogates these asymmetries through the lens of Comparative Political Economy, synthesising Developmental State Theory, Social Democratic Institutionalism, and inductively derived institutional patterns to construct an analytical framework adequate to the complexity of contemporary global financial governance. 
The paper makes four original contributions to the literature. First, we conduct the first comprehensive multi-continental institutional audit of nine major regional economic blocs, examining the African Union's Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), ECOWAS and its aborted ECO currency project, BRICS+, ASEAN, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), CELAC and Mercosur, the European Economic Area, and the Pacific regional architecture, within a unified analytical framework that tracks their stated objectives against demonstrated achievements. Second, we deploy scenario-modelled de-dollarisation simulations at 20%, 40%, and 60% thresholds, projecting impacts on trade finance costs, reserve currency composition, emerging market foreign exchange volatility, and global trade growth — an exercise absent from the existing reform literature at this level of specificity. Third, through composite scoring and cluster analysis of the top and bottom deciles of countries across six development metrics, we theorise the institutional determinants of development success and deprivation, drawing on patterns observed across Nordic social democracies, East Asian developmental states, and chronically underdeveloped frontier economies. Fourth, we synthesise findings into four reform pathways for the post-Bretton Woods order — a reformed Special Drawing Rights (SDR) system, a Plurilateral Monetary Compact, a regional reserve pooling architecture with CBDC interoperability, and comprehensive governance democratisation — with evidence-derived weights assigned to each pathway's feasibility and developmental impact. 
A dedicated sub-case analysis of Nigeria foregrounds the specific challenges and reform opportunities facing resource-rich, institutionally constrained African economies, drawing extensively on the scholarship and policy prescriptions of Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Soludo, and Sanusi Lamido Sanusi. The paper concludes that the current architecture is not merely suboptimal but structurally biased against the populations most in need of the stability and financing access it ostensibly provides, and that evidence-guided reform can achieve greater equity, financial stability, reduced USD dependency, and accelerated human development simultaneously rather than sequentially.

title: Beyond Prediction: Toward a Structural Complexity Science
affiliations: The Force Global Research Facility

detail.title: Beyond Prediction: Toward a Structural Complexity Science
detail.abstract: Complexity science successfully identified phenomena such as emergence, self-organization, adaptive dynamics, and nonlinear transitions, but did not identify the governing mechanism underlying them. This article proposes that these phenomena become interpretable when viewed through coherence physics and the Continuous Collective Capacity (CCC) architecture. Building on the invariant C + L + D = 1 (∀t), ΔC ≥ 0, complexity is redefined from an intrinsic property of systems to a relational condition between environmental variety and the coherence capacity of an intelligence field. From this perspective, emergence becomes the observable expression of coherence formation, self-organization becomes coherence convergence, and adaptive dynamics become expansions of metabolic capacity. Developed through design-science methodology and validated under controlled operational conditions, the framework offers a falsifiable reinterpretation of complexity science. Generalization beyond the tested environment remains subject to further empirical scrutiny.

title: Bank Ownership as a Political Instrument: Evidence from Chinese Local Governments
affiliations: Georgetown University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Shanghai Advanced Institute of Finance (SAIF)

detail.title: Bank Ownership as a Political Instrument: Evidence from Chinese Local Governments
detail.abstract: We study how local governments use equity stakes in banks as a political and fiscal instrument to expand off-budget credit. We develop a novel city-bank-year measure of Chinese local government ownership from banks' shareholder registries and link it to transaction-level borrowing by local government financing vehicles (LGFVs). We find that a one-standard-deviation increase in a local government's ownership stake in a bank raises that bank's credit to local government borrowers by 11%. We exploit a regulatory reform that forced private shareholders to unwind bank holdings to support a causal interpretation. This effect is stronger when political competition is intense, officials near the end of their terms, and fiscal constraints are tighter. Greater local-government ownership also makes LGFV investment more responsive to industry performance, yet these projects are more likely to fail, indicating that ownership directs credit to attractive industries at the cost of project quality.

title: Same Capital, Different Absorption: Foreign Venture Capital and Startup Acquisition Channels in Japan and Singapore

detail.abstract: Foreign venture capital (foreign VC) universally raises both the capital scale of portfolio startups and their propensity to become acquirers, yet the buyer-side acquisition channel into which this expanded capital is absorbed depends asymmetrically on the host country's institutions. We examine this proposition using 10,051 VC-backed startups in Japan and Singapore from PitchBook (2010–2024). After a strict screening filter, we estimate linear probability models with fixed effects and a timing-clean treatment that counts only foreign-VC exposure occurring before a firm's first acquisition, with standard errors firm-clustered for round-size models and HC3-robust for firm-level models. Foreign-VC involvement expands round size by about +99% in Japan and +106% in Singapore, and raises the pooled propensity to become an acquirer by +7.19pp (all p < 0.001). The institutional absorption of this propensity is asymmetric. Japan-favoring domestic absorption is negative and significant (foreign_vc_pre × Singapore on domestic acquisition = −5.66pp, p < 0.001) and survives controlling for pre-acquisition cumulative capital (−4.88pp, p = 0.001), distinguishing a capital-scale-independent institutional channel. By contrast, the Singapore cross-border interaction is +0.42pp (n.s.) in the preferred specification, and the cross-border main effect becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero once capital is controlled; Singapore's cross-border orientation is better interpreted as a composite of baseline ecosystem openness and capital scale-up than as an independent foreign-VC interaction. The central finding is universal capital scale-up plus asymmetric institutional absorption. We provide, to our knowledge, among the first firm-level estimates of whether VC-backed startups themselves become acquirers, and use a binary Japan–Singapore institutional-regime contrast to distinguish this asymmetric absorption. Findings reflect strong, mechanism-consistent associations rather than causal identification.

title: An Economic Analysis of Decentralized Commerce Trust Mechanism Based on Feynman Diagram Model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An Economic Analysis of Decentralized Commerce Trust Mechanism Based on Feynman Diagram Model
detail.abstract: Background: Centralized e-commerce platforms have resolved the trust problem in remote transactions through platform credit intermediation, but have created a new "trust black hole"-platforms can unilaterally modify rules, freeze funds, and abuse user data, leaving both merchants and buyers locked into the platform. Existing consortium blockchain solutions remain permissioned and fail to fundamentally resolve the trust issue. Research Question: How can we construct a programmable credit system that does not rely on any centralized platform, thereby rebuilding the physical foundation of commercial trust from an economic perspective? Methodology: This paper proposes the "Decentralized Commerce Feynman Diagram Model," introducing the formal methods of quantum field theory's Feynman diagrams into commercial transaction modeling. Through the creation and annihilation mechanisms of dNFT pairs (+/-credit quanta), local interaction vertices, and dual-world conservation laws, we establish a comprehensive trust cost analysis framework. Key Findings: 1. Trust Cost Quantification: The trust cost of remote transactions is 15-30% higher than face-to-face transactions (commissions 5-25% + return rates 10-30% + processing time 3-7 days). 2. Locality Value: Two local vertices (transaction contract + receipt contract) can reduce trust cost to $0.50/transaction (vs. platform commissions of 5-25%). 3. Game-Theoretic Stability: When delta x V_future >= V_fraud, honesty is the optimal strategy (empirical: at 96% discount factor, annual revenue $24,000 > fraud gain $5,000). 4. Cold-Start Feasibility: A three-dimensional initial credit generation mechanism (asset staking + verifiable credentials + guarantees) can provide new merchants with an initial credit score of 75 (out of 100). Policy Implications: Provides a theoretical basis for regulatory framework design, credit system standardization, and cross-border transaction trust mechanisms for decentralized commerce.

title: Trade Finance Gaps in Developing Economies: Barriers and Solutions

detail.title: Trade Finance Gaps in Developing Economies: Barriers and Solutions
detail.abstract: Trade finance is a critical enabler of international commerce, yet developing economies continue to face a persistent and widening gap in access to trade finance instruments. This paper examines the structural, regulatory, and institutional barriers that impede trade finance access in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs), with particular focus on Sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and Latin America. Drawing on data from the Asian Development Bank, the International Chamber of Commerce, the World Trade Organization, and the International Finance Corporation covering the period 2020-2025, this study estimates the global trade finance gap at approximately USD 2.5 trillion annually, with developing economies accounting for the largest share of unmet demand. Key barriers identified include stringent anti-money laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance requirements imposed by correspondent banks, inadequate domestic banking infrastructure, informational asymmetries, and limited collateral frameworks. The paper further analyzes the role of development finance institutions (DFIs), multilateral development banks (MDBs), and fintech-enabled solutions in bridging the gap. Policy recommendations are offered at the national, regional, and multilateral levels, including the adoption of harmonized digital trade documentation standards, expanded risk-sharing mechanisms, and targeted capacity-building programs for local financial institutions. The findings suggest that closing the trade finance gap requires coordinated institutional reform, regulatory recalibration, and strategic public-private investment.

detail.abstract:
Modern treatments of the tithe commonly reduce it to religious donation, legal obligation, institutional fundraising, or prosperity mechanism. While each captures part of the practice, none adequately explains the institutional and formational architecture created when sacred provision, spiritual authority, material dependence, pastoral responsibility, giver participation, and divine sovereignty operate together within the life of the Church. This paper introduces Ecclesiastical Economic Restraint as a doctrinal category and formally models it as an Ecclesiastical Provision–Dependence Mechanism: a sacred-economic architecture in which material provision sustains spiritual office while dependence constrains that office from becoming autonomous, coercive, entitled, economically captured, or self-grounded.

Employing biblical theology, systems analysis, and institutional economics, the paper traces sacred provision from Abram’s tithe to Melchizedek through patriarchal continuity, Mosaic codification, Levitical support, prophetic correction, the teachings of Christ, and New Testament patterns of generosity and pastoral provision. The analysis does not attempt to resolve denominational disagreement concerning the contemporary obligation or administration of the tithe. Instead, it asks a broader institutional question: what theological, economic, and ecclesiastical order emerges when spiritual authority is materially sustained through the participation of the community it serves?

The paper argues that the tithe performs both institutional and formational functions. Institutionally, provision sustains shepherding, teaching, worship, spiritual care, succession, and ecclesiastical continuity. Structurally, dependence upon God and the covenant community restrains spiritual office from becoming economically sovereign. Formationally, recurring participation trains the giver in source recognition, trust, remembrance, stewardship, and dependence upon divine wisdom. Read together, Deuteronomy 8:18 and Malachi 3:10 suggest that blessing is not merely distributive but formative: God may provide resources while also developing the wisdom, endurance, restraint, courage, and capacity necessary to administer greater responsibility faithfully.

The manuscript further develops the Widow’s Principle as a constraint upon pastoral perception. Christ’s valuation of the widow’s offering demonstrates that visible magnitude cannot serve as the Church’s complete measure of sacred value. A gift may be economically evaluated, but the giver must not be spiritually valued according to the magnitude of that gift. The gift belongs to ecclesiastical administration; the giver belongs to pastoral stewardship before God. The doctrine therefore rejects donor hierarchy, purchased access, wealth-based credibility, and the conversion of financial usefulness into perceived human worth.

These relationships are synthesized through a Multi-Axis Constraint Model consisting of Authority Constraint, Resource Constraint, Humility Emergence, Pastoral Perception Constraint, Participatory Formation, Wisdom Alignment, and Feedback Stability. Together, these constraints explain how provision may sustain ministry while dependence, humility, impartiality, voluntariness, accountability, and wisdom prevent accumulated capacity from becoming domination or disorder. To the author’s knowledge, this manuscript presents the first integrated systems-architecture model of the tithe as an Ecclesiastical Provision–Dependence Mechanism, unifying individual formation, institutional constraint, pastoral-perception restraint, failure-state propagation, and recurring ecclesiastical continuity within a single theological framework. The paper identifies seven recurrent failure states—donor capture, visibility bias, clerical entitlement, prosperity distortion, coercion, economic stratification, and institutional drift—and treats them as system-level distortions capable of propagating across ecclesiastical structures.

The paper’s principal contribution is to reframe the tithe as neither a one-directional transfer nor a mechanical exchange, but as a recurring ecclesiastical feedback architecture: provision sustains office; office shepherds and forms the community; formation strengthens wisdom and stewardship; stewardship renews willing participation; and the cycle returns both giver and shepherd to deeper dependence upon God. Properly ordered, the tithe functions as Ecclesiastical Economic Restraint—preserving authority without sovereignty, provision without ownership, increase without self-sufficiency, participation without coercion, difference without hierarchy, and institutional continuity without displacing God as the Church’s ultimate source.

keywords: Second Order Approximation in Time and Space

detail.abstract: he Fokker-Planck equation is fundamental to statistical mechanics, yet in settings with multiple state variables, anisotropic (cross-) diffusion, and jumps, conventional discretizations frequently produce non-physical negative probability densities. Building on the operator approach of "A. Itkin, Pricing derivatives under Levy models. Modern finite difference and pseudo-differential operators approach, Springer, 2017, ISBN 978-1-4939-6792-6", we introduce a family of "Diagonal Frog" discretizations whose spatial operators are eventually M-matrices (EM-matrices). Although these operators lack a local M-matrix structure, positivity of the directional sub-operators emerges in the spirit of Zeno's paradox: the matrix exponential, assembled as the limit of infinitely many ever-smaller substeps, is provably nonnegative after a short transient even though no single substep is. For the mixed-derivative block, whose generator is not eventually nonnegative, positivity instead rests on a factorized resolvent solver and holds conditionally, on an explicit step-size window; discrete mass is conserved exactly by the splitting for every step size. The resulting schemes are second-order accurate in time and space and require O(m 2 N + m 3) operations per time step, where m is the dimension of the Krylov subspace used to apply the exponential. As stress tests, we solve a two-dimensional anisotropic Fokker-Planck equation in the strong cross-diffusion regime against an exact Gaussian reference, a Kramers escape problem in a double-well potential, and an advection-dominated problem, and observe that the schemes remain stable, nonnegative, and mass-conservative for a wide range of Pécklet numbers (so, don't need any flux limiter). Finally, we extend the construction to multidimensional processes and to the backward Kolmogorov equation with jumps.

title: Meritocracy as a Structurally Embedded Ideology: A Comparative Sociological Analysis of Career Success in Pakistan and Global Corporations
affiliations: International Islamic University Islamabad, National Defence University and

detail.title: Meritocracy as a Structurally Embedded Ideology: A Comparative Sociological Analysis of Career Success in Pakistan and Global Corporations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: THE AUTHOR DECLARE NO CONFLICT OF INTEREST
declarations.funderStatement: THE RESERCH RECEIVED NO EXTERNAL FUNDING

detail.abstract:
Meritocracy is often touted as a fair and objective system whereby people are successful in their careers based on their talent and intelligence, and their efforts. But current sociological research is increasingly questioning this idea, as it is suggested that meritocracy can be an ideological tool that serves to legitimize structural inequality instead of eradicating it. This study explores the concept of meritocracy in a critical and comparative sociological perspective both in Pakistan and in the international corporations. The paper combines qualitative secondary analysis and theoretical interpretation with the Human Capital Theory, the Social Capital Theory and sociological critiques of meritocracy to examine the role of structural advantages in determining professional success. 
The study reveals that while there are different mechanisms of inequality that are visible in Pakistan and in the global corporations, both systems are responsible for the reproduction of inequalities through social capital, institutional privilege, educational stratification, and network-based advantages. Sifarish is a form of informal system in Pakistan while in global corporations it is manifested in credentialism, institutional prestige and cultural fit. The article states that meritocracy is a way of structuring inequality into a socially acceptable ideology, by attributing unequal outcomes solely to individual effort. 
The paper argues that career success is not just a matter of merit as opportunities for success are strongly influenced by class background, social networks, cultural capital and institutional structures. The study adds to the current debates about inequality, organizational sociology and stratification of the labor market, by questioning the notion of pure meritocracy in modern professional systems.

title: Riding the Hobby Horses: A Model of Taste-Driven Technology Diffusion
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Economics & Finance

detail.title: Riding the Hobby Horses: A Model of Taste-Driven Technology Diffusion
detail.abstract: This paper expounds on the demand forces driving the diffusion of general-purpose technology (GPT), in which cohort heterogeneity is the central engine of adoption dynamics. The GPT taste gap is the sufficient statistic ∆ which indexes all demand-side forces. We find that: (1) aggregate GPT demand is strictly increasing in ∆, generating demand waves at each cohort turnover; (2) the GPT adoption threshold is a strictly increasing function of δ, alongside an endogenous S-curve diffusion pattern; (3) the GPT adoption cost κ(µ t) and incremental R&D are strict complements; (4) aggregate output is superlinear in the adoption rate µ t , due to a capital reallocation effect; (5) the demand wave peak generically leads the S-curve inflexion point; and (6) GPT-firm equity prices carry a premium that rises with Θ. The calibration of the model demonstrates acceleration in the later phase of diffusion, the demand premium, and the taste-driven equity premium. A set of front-loaded subsidies and R&D subsidies is required to address adoption externalities.

title: Is Combination of Flexibility and Efficiency Good? Theory and Evidence
affiliations: Tianjin University of Finance & Economics, Tianjin University of Finance and Economics, Tianjin University of Finance and Economics and Tianjin University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Is Combination of Flexibility and Efficiency Good? Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: With the global proliferation of carbon emission trading systems, modern firms should navigate both dynamic environmental regulations and internal costlearning effects. This paper investigates how the interplay between regulatory stringency and learning efficiency shapes firm operations and social welfare under transferable (with banking) and non-transferable permit regimes. We develop a two-period analytical framework integrating regulation, abatement, production, and pricing decisions. Our theoretical analysis reveals a fundamental divergence in decision logics: while a non-transferable regime forces period-by-period compliance, the banking policy serves as a strategic buffer that allows firms to dynamically synchronize inter-temporal operations and amplify the investment effect of cost learning. Crucially, we identify a sharp policy counter-intuition: the combination of policy flexibility and high learning efficiency does not unequivocally enhance social welfare, it may paradoxically suppress welfare gains when a regulatory threshold is reached. To validate these analytical mechanisms, we conduct an empirical study using data from the U.S. Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI). The empirical findings strongly substantiate our theoretical predictions, confirming that the operational flexibility provided by permit banking significantly interacts with firms' cost-reduction trajectories and social welfare. This study bridges operational optimization and environmental economics, offering critical * Shuhua Zhang is the corresponding author.

title: Multi-Dimensional Framework for Assessing Farm Competitiveness in Bulgaria with Legal Structures
affiliations: Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University and Institute of Agricultural Economics

detail.title: Multi-Dimensional Framework for Assessing Farm Competitiveness in Bulgaria with Legal Structures
detail.abstract: This study challenges traditional economic models of farm competitiveness by highlighting the underexamined role of legal structures. It argues that a farm’s governing structure significantly impacts its ability to thrive in the market. The authors propose a novel framework for assessing farm competitiveness that encompasses three key dimensions: economic efficiency, financial health, and governance effectiveness. This framework is then applied to evaluate various agricultural governing structures in Bulgaria. A multi-layered evaluation system with four pillars is employed to assess competitiveness across these structures. The research reveals a generally positive competitiveness landscape for Bulgarian agriculture, with cooperatives demonstrating the highest level of competitiveness. However, some critical areas for improvement are identified, including low productivity, income, financial security, and adaptation to environmental challenges. The study also finds that a significant portion of Bulgarian farms struggle with low competitiveness. The research emphasizes the need for targeted interventions to address these weaknesses, including public support and improved management practices. Additionally, it highlights the importance of restructuring struggling farms and implementing better management approaches. Furthermore, the study underscores the crucial role of government support in preventing farm closures. Finally, the research reveals that farm size, specialization, market focus, and ecological location all play a role in competitiveness, but the significance of these factors varies depending on the specific governing structure employed.

title: From Stability Dependence to Capability Self-Reliance: Pathways to Career Security among Students at an Applied University in China

detail.title: From Stability Dependence to Capability Self-Reliance: Pathways to Career Security among Students at an Applied University in China

No personally identifiable information was collected, and the data were used only in aggregate form. No formal external ethics approval was obtained for this minimal-risk student survey.

detail.abstract: Career security is often understood as a labor-market outcome: whether a graduate can obtain a stable job after leaving college. This paper reframes career security as a pre-labor-market judgment formed during the transition from university to work. Drawing on an anonymous survey of 106 undergraduate students at Wuhan College, an applied university in China, we examine how students evaluate their academic confidence, skill readiness, employment prospects, and psychological resilience. The analysis shows a clear structural imbalance. Academic security is the strongest dimension (M = 3.42), while skill security (M = 2.65) and employment security (M = 2.41) fall below the neutral midpoint of a five-point Likert scale. Core items reveal that 59.43% of respondents tend to seek stability through civil-service or other public-sector paths, 66.98% report skill anxiety, and only 24.53% believe that they can make clear and autonomous career plans. Reliability analysis for the main scale indicates high internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.945, N = 100). We interpret these patterns through four mechanisms: practice-experience deficits, major-structure differences, family-resource constraints, and the limits of standardized school support. The paper argues that career security for applied-university students should be built less around dependence on stable organizations and more around capability self-reliance: transferable skills, visible project evidence, career planning agency, and psychological resilience.

title: Ethics Suppression in AI Development: A Comparative Case Study of Responsible AI under Competitive Pressure

detail.title: Ethics Suppression in AI Development: A Comparative Case Study of Responsible AI under Competitive Pressure
detail.abstract: This study analyses governance tensions among Google, OpenAI, Meta, and Microsoft to explain how ethics suppression may emerge in competitive AI development environments. While responsible AI frameworks, ethical principles, safety initiatives, and governance mechanisms have expanded rapidly across the technology sector, considerably less a ention has been paid to how ethical concerns function under conditions of accelerated development and strategic rivalry. The paper introduces the concept of ethics suppression in AI development to explain how ethical oversight may remain formally present even as its practical authority over development and deployment decisions weakens. Unlike existing literature on ethics washing, which focuses primarily on symbolic external signalling, the paper examines the internal organisational dynamics through which ethical authority may weaken despite continued institutional visibility. Drawing on corporate governance documents, public statements, investigative reporting, and documented governance controversies, the analysis identifies recurring pa erns involving constrained escalation authority, temporal compression, deployment urgency, and governance fragmentation. The findings suggest that intensified competition may reduce the practical impact of ethical oversight, even within organisations with mature responsible AI structures. The paper contributes to responsible AI governance literature by introducing the concept of ethics suppression and an operationalsuppression lens to examine how ethical authority is preserved or diminished under competitive pressure. The study argues that the central challenge of responsible AI governance may no longer lie primarily in establishing ethical frameworks, but in maintaining ethical influence when deployment incentives intensify.

title: Non-stationary Stochastic Optimization: Adaptive Stochastic Gradient Descent Algorithm and Applications in Operations
affiliations: The Hong Kong Polytechnic University,  and

detail.title: Non-stationary Stochastic Optimization: Adaptive Stochastic Gradient Descent Algorithm and Applications in Operations
detail.abstract: Many operations research problems involve sequential decision making in stochastic environments whose underlying distributions change over time. In this paper, we develop a gradient-based modeling-and-algorithmic framework for online stochastic convex optimization under a variation-budget constraint on the changing distributions. To adapt to the unknown variation budget $V_T$, we propose an Adaptive Stochastic Gradient Descent (AdaSGD) algorithm. This algorithm maintains multiple SGD learners calibrated to different hypothetical variation levels and switches to the learners with higher-variation levels by comparing the cumulative costs of the active and inactive learners. For general convex objectives, AdaSGD achieves dynamic regret of order $\widetilde{O}(T^{2/3} V_T^{1/3})$, matching the optimal regret rate up to logarithmic factors. We then apply this framework to three important classes of problems in operations. For a non-perishable inventory control problem, we modify the AdaSGD algorithm and establish a regret upper bound against the clairvoyant optimal inventory policy of order $\widetilde{O}(T^{2/3} V_T^{1/3})$. To account for the effect of inventory carryover, we construct two non-stationary queueing processes and bound the waiting times by carefully analyzing the lengths of their busy periods. We also show that this regret order is tight by proving a matching regret lower bound. For the first-price auction bidding problem and online portfolio selection problem, we obtain dynamic regret guarantees of the same order through, respectively, a convex bidding reformulation and an entropic mirror descent variant. Across the three applications, numerical experiments show that our proposed algorithms consistently achieve strong empirical performance and computational efficiency. The framework is further extended to both strongly convex and time-dependent cost functions.

title: Where do Racial Achievement Gaps Come From? A Hierarchical Decomposition of Sorting and Within-Classroom Gaps in Brazilian Education
affiliations: Insper Institute of Education and Research and

detail.title: Where do Racial Achievement Gaps Come From? A Hierarchical Decomposition of Sorting and Within-Classroom Gaps in Brazilian Education
detail.abstract: A large literature worldwide decomposes racial and ethnic achievement gaps into between-and within-school components. However, because ethnic groups are commonly concentrated in some geographical regions, these between-school effects might arise either because students attend different schools in the same region or because they live in different regions. We propose a methodology that decomposes achievement gaps into a within-classroom component and a four-level hierarchical sorting structure across states, municipalities, schools, and classrooms. We apply our methodology to Brazilian data covering approximately five million students in 5th, 9th, and 12th grade. We find that the black/white gap (0.54-0.61 SD in mathematics) and the mixed-race/white gap (0.25-0.38 SD) have qualitatively different structures. For black students, withinclassroom disadvantage net of socioeconomic controls explains 38-42% of the gap, while for mixed-race students, sorting explains 56-65%. Geographic sorting between states and municipalities accounts for 22-36% of the gap and is of similar magnitude as the between-school component. The decomposition maps directly onto the administrative layers at which education policy operates and quantifies the share of the gap each policy lever can, in principle, reach. Our results show that no single intervention is sufficient on its own to eliminate racial disparities in test-scores.

detail.title: Benchmarking Output Efficiency as a Tool to Reduce the Rate of Tariff Increases and Promote Access to Affordable Petroleum Products: A Case of the Regulated Petroleum Storage Facilities Market of South Africa

keywords: Data Envelopment Analysis and Stochastic Frontier Analysis

detail.abstract: The paper explores the use of benchmarking efficiency or optimum industry performance of similar firms in an industry (petroleum pipelines facilities) to advance the efforts of ensuring access to affordable petroleum products. The variables employed include volumes achieved from a certain capacity size utilisation, capacity size, and tariffs. The field of regulatory economics for utility of petroleum facilities is complex and can sometimes be specific to particular needs of each country rather than offering a collective approach to industry issues. This is evident from the lack of literature exploring the role or impact of efficiency or the lack thereof on fuel prices. The paper will provide significant contribution towards the much needed literature on this topic. In terms of the methodology, the paper will employ the data envelopment analysis and stochastic frontier analysis methods of measuring and benchmarking efficiency. Subsequently, a comparative analysis will be conducted in order to ascertain whether efficient petroleum storage facilities, in terms of maximising the use of inputs (capacity size of storage facilities) in order to produce the optimal output possible (volumes of petroleum products stored at storage facilities, contribute towards the advancement of affordable petroleum prices downstream. The data will be collected from NERSA and treated with confidentiality and sensitivity undertakings. The conclusions to be drawn from results will then be used to formulate policy recommendations for the National Energy Regulator of South Africa, which is primarily responsible for the petroleum pipeline, storage and loading facilities market as well the relevant government department responsible for the South African petroleum industry.

title: Integration of Ukrainian Grain Markets with Foreign Markets During Russia’s Invasion of Ukraine
affiliations: Warsaw University of Life Sciences, Warsaw University of Life Sciences, National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine, National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine and National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine

detail.title: Integration of Ukrainian Grain Markets with Foreign Markets During Russia’s Invasion of Ukraine
detail.abstract: The paper aims to evaluate the implications of the Russian-Ukrainian conflict for the strength and nature of the integration of Ukrainian grain markets with world markets. The empirical research is based on the theoretical foundations of spatial market integration and the spatial market equilibrium model. According to them, changes in the integration of Ukrainian and world wheat, corn, and barley markets are evaluated via fluctuations in trade flow volumes, changes in trade costs and price co-movement. To analyze trade implications, monthly trade flow volumes, trade shares, and trade concentration measures during the conflict were compared with expected values assuming no war. To evaluate the implications of the conflict for trade costs, the authors analyzed differences between Ukrainian and world grain prices. Relying on the weekly price series, the price co-movement was assessed using the autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) and Granger instantaneous causality test. The results show that the strength of the integration of Ukrainian grain markets with world markets has deteriorated due to the conflict. It is confirmed by the decrease in the grain export volumes from Ukraine, the increase in price differences, and the lack of significant price transmission between Ukrainian and global grain markets since the war outbreak in February 2022. Moreover, the nature of the market integration has changed. One can observe a growing role of the European Union countries in the Ukrainian grain export share and changes in the Ukrainian grain export concentration. Such behaviour is in line with the theoretical foundation of the spatial market equilibrium model and theory of international integration.

title: Differentiation of Profitability of Traditional and Innovative Potatoes Cultivation in Poland
affiliations: Warsaw University of Life Sciences, Warsaw University of Life Sciences, Warsaw University of Life Sciences, Plant Breeding and Acclimatization Institute National Research Institute, Plant Breeding and Acclimatization Institute National Research Institute and Plant Breeding and Acclimatization Institute National Research Institute

detail.title: Differentiation of Profitability of Traditional and Innovative Potatoes Cultivation in Poland
detail.abstract: The aim of the research was to determine the costs and profitability of traditional and innovative potatoes cultivation in Poland. The experimental field trials of selected potato varieties in various variants were carried out between 2021 and 2022. The applied variants of experiments included potatoes cultivation according to traditional and innovative methods, i.e. in commercial conditions (high intensity of inputs and costs, including fertilization with mineral fertilizers and synthetic plant protection products) and in the absence of fertilization and plant protection, or only with the use of interaction with beneficial microorganisms. For economic calculations, there were applied methods of profitability of potatoes production for the evaluation of various production variants, calculation of production costs and assessment of production profit. The research material consisted of the results of field experiments carried out as part of the international PotatoMETAbiome project for 11 potato varieties and six variants of the experiment in fields located in the north of Poland. Based on the research, it was found that the average potatoes production costs in 2021 and 2022 decreased for traditional variants and increased for innovative variants. In 2021, the lowest production costs were for the variant without fertilization and plant protection products and innovative variants. In turn, in 2022, the lowest production costs were for traditional variants, i.e., with fertilization and protection, and without fertilization with protection, as well as with fertilization and without chemical protection, and without fertilization and without chemical protection. In all years under consideration and for all variants, potatoes cultivation was profitable. The potatoes production profitability ratios during the years under analysis decreased for innovative variants, while they increased for variants with intensive production. It was found that an innovative strategy of potatoes production with the use of beneficial microorganisms may be an economically justified alternative to changing production, market, and political conditions.

title: When the Monitor Learns from the Monitored: Endogenous Algorithmic Accuracy and the Lock-in of Hiring Corruption

detail.title: When the Monitor Learns from the Monitored: Endogenous Algorithmic Accuracy and the Lock-in of Hiring Corruption

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is theoretical and computational. It involves no human participants, animal subjects, or identifiable personal data, and therefore ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly deploy AI scoring systems to discipline the managers who make hiring decisions. Unlike a human auditor, an algorithmic monitor is retrained on the data the organization itself generates, and the managers it is meant to discipline are the ones who generate that data. We build a dynamic principal–agent model of hiring corruption in which the monitor's effective accuracy is an equilibrium object rather than a technological parameter. Each period, a manager facing connected candidates chooses screening effort and whether to corrupt the hire; corrupt hires that escape audit re-enter the AI's training data as mislabeled successes; the monitor's accuracy next period is determined by the contamination of its training labels. When the feedback is steep, the dynamical system is bistable: a high-accuracy, low-corruption governance steady state coexists with a low-accuracy, high-corruption lock-in steady state in which the algorithm has learned to score connected candidates favorably, institutionalizing the behavior it was deployed to prevent. Audit coverage acts as a bifurcation parameter. Audits in this model correct labels rather than punish, and above a critical coverage a* the lock-in state disappears through a saddle-node bifurcation and governance becomes globally stable. The model also delivers a data dividend of deterrence: at any stable steady state, the long-run effect of a penalty increase exceeds its static deterrence effect by the factor 1/(1−Ψ'(α∞)) ≥ 1 (strict wherever feedback is active), because deterring corruption today also cleans the data the monitor learns from tomorrow. Agent-based simulations in which an actual classifier is retrained each period on endogenously generated labels, with no assumed accuracy dynamics, exhibit the loop's signature: emergent monitor degradation under polluted feedback, collapse to outright ranking inversion when audits vanish, relapse after model resets that leave the label regime unchanged, and a large measured data dividend, the same penalty raise ending with corruption nearly four times higher when the monitor is frozen. The simulations also discipline the theory: with a regularized learner, steady states are unique given audit policy, history washes out, and the deepest collapses occur in noisy-outcome environments, consistent with the steep-map condition the theory identifies for bistability.

title: Networks in Finance: Foundations and Frontiers
affiliations: Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Jerusalem School of Business Administration,  and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Finance Area

detail.title: Networks in Finance: Foundations and Frontiers

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted for publication in the Annual Review of Financial Economics

detail.abstract: Networks in finance shape how value is created and risks emerge, both systemic and systematic. We survey how different networks, including production, banking, directors, and information networks, propagate micro shocks and transmit them to broader levels of aggregation. First, we synthesize the literature on the efficiency-stability trade-off governing systemic risk: interconnections transmit gains, liquidity, and knowledge, but create channels for contagion. Beyond the foundational focus on within-network transmission, we extend the discussion to across-network spillovers. Second, moving from systemic to systematic risk, we show how network topology drives the stochastic discount factor, affecting factors and expected returns. We also trace how networks form and evolve, dynamically generating new sources of risk. By adopting a macro perspective that unifies distinct networks into an overarching network-of-networks (meta-network), we focus on shared propagation mechanisms and outline directions for future research, including how networks may evolve with the rise of AI, intangibles, and deglobalization.

title: Natural Resources, National Income, and Resource Movement Effect under a Rent Seeking Monopoly
affiliations: Fukuoka University - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Natural Resources, National Income, and Resource Movement Effect under a Rent Seeking Monopoly
detail.abstract: In this paper, a new model is developed by referring to the literature of Dutch disease and rent-seeking for explaining how a natural resource boom in energy sector decreases national income and induces resource movement effect under a rent seeking monopoly. In the rent seeking monopoly model, it is shown that resource movement effect certainly occurs during the boom where labor inputs will move to energy sector from services sector. Moreover, the boom facilitates rent-seeking and decreases national income.

contentType.other: Methodology document accompanying an interactive data dashboard

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a comparative index of AI regulatory environments across seven jurisdictions: Isle of Man, Singapore, Estonia, Jersey, United Kingdom, European Union, and United States. The index assesses six dimensions: Regulatory Clarity, Speed of Policy Response, National AI Strategy Maturity, Business Environment, Government AI Adoption, and International Positioning. All scores are derived from published sources including the OECD AI Policy Observatory, Stanford HAI AI Index, Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index, and primary government documentation.

The index addresses a systematic gap in existing benchmarks: the OECD, Stanford HAI, and Oxford Insights indices cover sovereign states only. Crown Dependencies including the Isle of Man, Jersey, and Guernsey are excluded despite maintaining independent regulatory frameworks and distinct digital economy strategies. This paper corrects that absence.

Key findings: Singapore ranks first (88/100), followed by Estonia (83/100) and the Isle of Man (73/100). The Isle of Man's Business Environment scores 9.0/10, the highest of any jurisdiction assessed. Its structural ceiling is International Positioning at 5.0/10, a direct consequence of non-sovereign status preventing multilateral AI governance participation. The European Union scores highest on Regulatory Clarity (9.0/10) but the European Parliament Research Service estimates compliance costs at €29,000–€300,000+ per AI system, reflected in its overall index score of 65/100.

An interactive Tableau Public dashboard accompanies this methodology document. Full source citations and raw data are published alongside the dashboard.

title: A Lifting-and-Splitting Framework for Risk-Averse Distributionally Robust Multi-Item Newsvendor Problems
affiliations: , , The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen - Shenzhen Research Institute of Big Data and Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business

detail.title: A Lifting-and-Splitting Framework for Risk-Averse Distributionally Robust Multi-Item Newsvendor Problems
detail.abstract: Risk-averse distributionally robust multi-item newsvendor problems provide a fundamental model for inventory decision making under demand uncertainty, limited distributional information, and downside-risk concerns. In this paper, we study this problem under mean-covariance demand ambiguity, and the decision maker maximizes worst-case conditional value-at-risk of profit, capturing both limited distributional information and downside-risk concerns. While cross-item demand correlations are important for portfolio-level inventory decisions, preserving the full covariance structure leads to an NP-hard problem and becomes computationally challenging for large assortments. We develop a lifting-and-splitting framework that combines exact reformulation, scalable approximation, and performance guarantees. First, we derive an exact semidefinite programming reformulation based on the constrained Boolean quadric polytope, replacing exponentially many positive semidefinite constraints in the classical dual formulation with exponentially many linear constraints. Second, we propose a correlation-splitting approximation that partitions items into clusters, preserves within-cluster covariance information, and relaxes cross-cluster dependence. We establish exactness conditions and derive an explicit cluster-wise upper bound on the optimality gap. We further show that, in the two-cluster case, the approximation becomes increasingly accurate when one cluster has uniformly small demand variability, motivating a simple variance-based splitting rule. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved exact-solution tractability, strong approximation quality, and scalability to large instances.

title: Natural Resources and Rent Seeking Collusion in the Context of Dutch Disease
affiliations: Fukuoka University - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Natural Resources and Rent Seeking Collusion in the Context of Dutch Disease
detail.abstract: A new model is proposed in this paper by concentrating on the Dutch disease phenomenon along with rent seeking to demonstrate how a natural resource abundance (or a resource boom) affects resource movement and national income under rent seeking collusion in the energy sector. Dutch disease and rent seeking problems are studied under the natural resource curse theory which states that countries with natural resources usually perform worse than resourcepoor countries. The resource movement is considered one of the effects of the Dutch disease. The resource movement occurrence or the movement of labor inputs from services to the energy sector depends on the degree of the boom. The boom may also facilitate rent seeking depending on its degree and the number of firms in the energy sector. In the duopoly case (n=2), a sufficiently small degree of the boom is necessary for rent seeking to be facilitated. However, with more than two firms (n>2), rent seeking activities will not happen because profits in collusion will be less than those without collusion in the model. Hence, the paper analyzes rent seeking by concentrating on duopoly results (n=2). The impact of the boom on national income depends on parameter values.

publicationDetails.detailsText: GEMDEV - CONTROVERSIES and DEBATES WORKING PAPERS

detail.abstract:
For nearly three years, GEMDEV (Group for the Study of Globalization and Development) has been supporting the scientific coordination of the CoRe (Communities and Resilience) program. The CoRe program, a multi-year partnership led by Secours Catholique–Caritas France (SC-CF), brings together 23 partners from 18 countries and aims to promote a just ecological transition by strengthening the capacity for action of local actors. This document is part of the partnership between the ARPOP (Public Policy Network Analysis) team at GEMDEV and Caritas Bangladesh on the Advancement of Land Rights of Indigenous Communities (ALOC) project. This partnership, running from September 2024 to September 2025, is part of the CoRe program. Within this framework, the GEMDEV-ARPOP team has developed an experimental relational assessment module: a tool for monitoring and improving project governance, based on the analysis of networks of relationships between partners. The ALOC project, now in its third phase, was chosen as a pilot site for testing this module due to its rich network of stakeholders (community organizations, national NGOs, public institutions, etc.) and its deep roots in the territorial dynamics of land rights and ecological justice. This document reports on the experience of the relational assessment module, from its development and implementation to the results observed and the strengths and weaknesses they reveal in the collective governance of the ALOC project. 

Relational assessment relies on network analysis, which maps the relationships impacting project progress: information exchange, collaboration, perceived impact of collaboration, and ideological affinity. The results include maps of the relationships between all actors identified as project stakeholders. By using measures such as centrality, density, and betweenness, it becomes possible to objectify relational mechanisms such as influence, cohesion, power, information asymmetries, and obstacles hindering effective coordination. The results also include a section on actors' perceptions of a just ecological transition and the defense of Indigenous rights, in order to assess their coherence and impact on network cohesion. The joint interpretation of the results of the relational analysis of the ALOC-3 project's partner network identifies several obstacles and factors promoting coordination and cooperation among stakeholders. A brief summary of the results is presented here; they are detailed in Part 4 of this report.
+ A widely shared ideological foundation on the interdependence between land rights and environmental preservation
+ A moderate but sufficient relational density to ensure information flow and coordination
+ The existence of recognized bridging and central actors who can ensure inter-scale and inter-type connections
+ Participatory governance driven by local organizations, creating a committed "core group"
- Persistent asymmetries in mutual recognition and the perceived impact of collaborations
- A moderate but real segmentation between local and national scales
- Limited and peripheral engagement of government actors, despite their institutional power
- A gap between ideological convergence and effective collaboration among some actors

title: The Azores Index (A-Index): Balancing Peak Performance and Portfolio Density in Citation Analysis
affiliations: Royal Statistical Society

detail.title: The Azores Index (A-Index): Balancing Peak Performance and Portfolio Density in Citation Analysis
detail.abstract: Although widely adopted, established metrics like the h-index frequently flatten variation beyond the core threshold, while the traditional average citation count remains susceptible to individual outliers and portfolio expansion. We propose the Azores Index (A-index), a novel metric that partitions an author's publication list into three distinct tiers: the top 3 papers, the middle third, and the remainder. The index averages the citations of the top 3 papers, adds the total citations of the middle third, and normalizes the result by the total number of publications. This design simultaneously rewards exceptional impact and consistent mid-level productivity, while strongly penalizing dilution from low-cited papers. We formally define the index, discuss its mathematical properties, and provide illustrative comparisons with established metrics.

title: Rethinking Monetary Policy
affiliations: Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA)

detail.title: Rethinking Monetary Policy
detail.abstract: Rethinking Monetary Policy: The Case for NGDP Targeting in Britain argues that the Bank of England’s current inflation-targeting framework is ill-suited to managing supply-side shocks and periods of financial instability, contributing to economic volatility and policy errors. The paper proposes replacing inflation targeting with a nominal gross domestic product (NGDP) targeting regime, which focuses on stabilizing total nominal spending in the economy. According to the author, NGDP targeting would better accommodate both demand and supply shocks, reduce uncertainty, and enhance transparency and credibility in monetary policymaking. The paper also advocates the development of a nominal GDP futures market and improved communication mechanisms to facilitate implementation. Overall, it contends that a rules-based NGDP framework would promote long-term economic stability, support sustainable growth, and restore confidence in the Bank of England’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability.

title: Frozen-Opponent Evaluation and Live-Update Continuation in Algorithmic Pricing

detail.title: Frozen-Opponent Evaluation and Live-Update Continuation in Algorithmic Pricing
detail.abstract: Holding a pricing rival fixed and allowing it to continue updating define different evaluation objects. We study this distinction in a Calvano-style Bertrand-logit duopoly. A DQN entrant is trained against ten independently trained mature Q-learning incumbents, with three DQN initializations per incumbent. After training, the same entrant-incumbent pair is evaluated with the incumbent either frozen or permitted to resume Q-updates. The entrant profit advantage is positive in 9 of 10 frozen-checkpoint means but only 6 of 10 live-update means; entrant own profit falls in all 10 matched comparisons. Separately, six configured learners spanning public reward feedback, known-payoff counterfactuals, Q-supervised auxiliary objectives, and direct Q-update-model access remain below the ten-seed mature Q-vs-Q reference in mean own profit and mean market price. These finite-budget results show that evaluation protocol is part of the estimand and that the tested richer configurations do not reproduce the Q-vs-Q high-price convention. Lower logged prices raise model-implied consumer surplus; total-welfare conclusions depend on the learner and on a binned-trajectory approximation.

title: Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence for Autonomous Enterprise Automation

detail.title: Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence for Autonomous Enterprise Automation
